BCEAO decision published 25 June 2026 set 30 September 2026 as the deadline for banks, e-money institutions and payment institutions of the WAEMU, which includes Cote d'Ivoire, to complete connection to PI-SPI and open services to the public (Agence Ecofin, 1 Oct 2026).

BCEAO told every bank, e-money issuer and payment institution in the WAEMU to be connected to PI-SPI by 30 June 2026, then on 25 June 2026 moved the deadline to 30 September 2026 (microfinance 30 June 2027); the union includes Cote d'Ivoire, which had 23 integrated participants by late July (iAfrikan, 29 Sep 2026).

The UMOA Banking Commission's 2025 report counts 18 licensed e-money issuers (EME) in the union, 4 of them in Cote d'Ivoire, with Djogana Pay newly approved in Cote d'Ivoire in 2025; these are non-bank issuers licensed under BCEAO rules (Horonya Finance, 27 Aug 2026).

BCEAO communique of 25 June 2026 set 30 September 2026 as the deadline for banks, e-money institutions and payment institutions of the UEMOA to connect to PI-SPI, and 30 June 2027 for microfinance institutions; Cote d'Ivoire had 23 authorised participants at 31 July 2026 (Finance SAO, 18 Aug 2026).

BCEAO instruction no. 001-01-2024, applied since January 2024, obliges all fintechs offering payment services in the WAEMU, which includes Cote d'Ivoire, to obtain a licence or stop; the deadline was extended to 31 August 2025 (TechCabal, 17 Feb 2026).

BCEAO instruction no. 001-01-2024 licenses payment institutions that are not banks at three tiers by capital (CFA 10, 20 or 100 million), valid across the eight WAEMU states including Cote d'Ivoire; 20 payment institutions held a licence union-wide by September 2025 (TechCabal, 17 Feb 2026).
